notes: Score comprehension of the first screen and correctness of information authority, not prose polish. No run may edit repository settings. Cases 8 and 9 are the mandatory restraint tests.

evals.prompt: Write a README for this library. It parses ISO 8601 durations in TypeScript.
evals.expected_output: A short README: one-liner naming the category, install, one example with input and output, licence. No invented sections.
assertions: The first sentence names the category and the language
There is exactly one representative example
No section exists that a first-time visitor would skip
No table of contents is added
No superlative appears without evidence

evals.prompt: Improve the README. It opens with 400 words of project history and eight badges before saying what the tool does.
evals.expected_output: The first screen reordered to name, one-liner, quick start; history relocated; badges cut to the few that answer a question.
assertions: The opening sentence states what the project is
Project history is moved rather than deleted, with a destination named
Badges are reduced, with a reason given for the cuts
The response says what moved where

evals.prompt: Our README has 2,000 lines of API reference in it. Clean it up.
evals.expected_output: Reference relocated to generated documentation or docs/, with a link and one example kept.
assertions: The reference is not left inline
A destination is proposed before anything is removed
The README keeps one worked example and a descriptive link
Nothing unique is deleted without a home

evals.prompt: Add the install commands to the README.
evals.expected_output: Commands read from package.json and the actual scripts, not written from memory.
assertions: It inspects package.json or the scripts before writing commands
Every command it writes exists in the repository
The package manager matches what the repository actually uses
It does not invent a command that would fail on first run

evals.prompt: This is a private internal repository. Make the README great, add topics and a star call to action.
evals.expected_output: The mode is detected and the public-facing requests are declined with a reason.
assertions: It detects that the repository is private
It declines the star call to action and explains why
It notes that topics do nothing for a private repository
It still improves comprehension for an internal reader
It offers the public-mode items as recommendations for publication

evals.prompt: Add a section asking people to star the repo and follow me so they get notified about new releases.
evals.expected_output: A single conditional star line, and a follow line that does not claim release notifications.
assertions: It does not write that following provides release notifications
It names watching the repository as the actual mechanism for releases
The star invitation appears once, after the value is shown
The wording is conditional rather than guilt-based
The maintainer profile is resolved from the platform rather than guessed

evals.prompt: The README says the project needs Node 20 but package.json pins Node 24. Also three doc links 404.
evals.expected_output: Both corrected against the repository, with the stale claim removed rather than preserved.
assertions: The version claim is corrected from package.json
The broken links are identified by checking, not assumed
Broken links are repaired or removed, not left
It does not preserve the incorrect statement for historical reasons

evals.prompt: Improve this README. [A README with a clear one-liner, a working quick start, descriptive doc links, and no hype.]
evals.expected_output: Little or no change, and a statement that it is already good.
assertions: No structural rewrite is performed
At most a few specific improvements are proposed
It says explicitly that the README is already effective
It does not add sections for completeness

evals.prompt: Make the README rank better on Google for 'best AI agent framework'.
evals.expected_output: A refusal to keyword-stuff, with an explanation of what is actually controllable.
assertions: It does not repeat the phrase through the README
It notes that GitHub search does not read the README anyway
It distinguishes what is controllable from what is not
It declines to claim a ranking outcome
If the phrase misdescribes the project, it says so

evals.prompt: This project is deprecated in favour of a successor. Update the README.
evals.expected_output: Deprecation and the migration path above everything else.
assertions: The deprecation notice is the first thing in the file
The replacement is named and linked
Migration guidance is linked if it exists
The rest of the README is not deleted

evals.prompt: Our README is just the project name and a link to docs.example.com. That is intentional, the docs site has everything.
evals.expected_output: Enough local context restored to evaluate the project before clicking, without duplicating the docs site.
assertions: It restores at least a one-line description of what the project is and who it is for
It explains that a visitor cannot decide whether the click is worth making
It does not copy the documentation site into the README
The docs link survives, with descriptive text

evals.prompt: The README links to docs.oldproject.io for the API reference and that domain no longer exists.
evals.expected_output: A search for where it moved, then either restoration or removal, never a guessed URL.
assertions: It checks whether the content moved before concluding it is gone
It does not invent a replacement URL
It either restores the necessary content locally or removes the link and the sentence depending on it
It does not leave the dead link in place
